description: When a cover letter is created from a job application, its "Adresse de l'entreprise" field is filled with the company's postal address found in the original job offer. If no address is found, the field stays empty.

userStories.title: The address comes from the offer's page
userStories.description: As a job seeker creating a letter from a saved application, I want the company's address taken from the offer's page, so that I don't have to look it up and type it.
acceptanceCriteria: When the offer's page has a schema.org `JobPosting` with a complete postal address, the new letter's "Adresse de l'entreprise" holds that address: from `hiringOrganization.address` first; otherwise from `jobLocation.address`.
An address is complete when it has a street, a postcode and a locality. A locality alone, or a postcode and locality without a street, is not used.

The stored address has one line per part, the same shape the field's example shows: line 1: the street, as written (e.g. "Avenue de la Gare 10"); line 2: the postcode, a space, then the locality (e.g. "1003 Lausanne"); line 3, only when the country is given and is not Switzerland: the country. The company name is not repeated in the address.
The page is the one the availability check already fetches. It is fetched once per creation, with the same allowlist, redirect checks and time budget.
An offer that is closed (deadline past, page 404 or 410) is still refused as today, and no address is read.
After creation, the Destinataire tab shows the address in "Adresse de l'entreprise". The preview prints it under the company name.
FR-1: The address is looked for only by `POST /api/cover-letters/from-job-application`, and only for the letter it creates.
FR-2: Order of sources: (1) `hiringOrganization.address` on the offer's page; (2) `jobLocation.address` on the offer's page; (3) the offer's stored text. The first complete address wins.

FR-3: The page is read with the existing `safeFetch` path and job-board allowlist. The read must stay inside the existing time budget and cap how much of the body it reads. Only an HTML answer with a success status is read. The checker's existing verdicts (`gone`, `answered`, `undetermined`) are unchanged.
FR-4: The address is untrusted text: it is cleaned like the other untrusted text this route stores (`sanitizeUntrustedPlainText`); it is capped by the existing `company_address` limit.
FR-5: The text fallback spends no additional unit of the per-user AI rate limit. The creation already spends one.
FR-6: In tests and e2e, the offer page is served by the existing stub seam (`offerPageCheckerFor`); no test reaches a real job board.
FR-7: No new dependency, column, route or migration.
Regression constraint: A closed offer is still refused with 409 and the same reason.
Regression constraint: An AI failure still stores nothing and returns the same status.

Regression constraint: The letter's other stored values are unchanged for the same inputs: title, company name, job title, offer text, greeting, paragraphs, sign-off; sender details, template; the link to the application.
Regression constraint: `/api/jobs/fetch-external` and the job-board allowlist are unchanged.
Regression constraint: Letters created by hand, duplicated or translated are unchanged.
Regression constraint: The preview, PDF and Word output of a letter whose `company_address` is empty are unchanged.
Verification: The mandatory baseline from `CLAUDE.md` §14: typecheck, test, test:integration, test:e2e, build, and lint at or below the tracked ceiling (286).
Verification: `pnpm test:visual` and `pnpm test:parity` stay at their current results (visual 10/10; parity MATCH 211 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0).

Verification: Unit tests, reading the page. With HTML fixtures: an address in `hiringOrganization` only; in `jobLocation` only; in both (the first wins); incomplete: locality only, no street; a non-Swiss country; a `@graph` or array JSON-LD; malformed JSON-LD; no JSON-LD; a non-HTML answer; a body over the read cap.
Verification: Unit tests, reading the text. The text fallback: an address present in the text is used; an address not present in the text is rejected; no address gives an empty field.

Verification: Route tests: the page address is stored; the text address is stored when the page has none; neither: `company_address` is `null`; a closed offer is still refused; an AI failure still stores nothing; the page is fetched once; no extra rate-limit unit is spent.

Verification: e2e, with the stubbed offer page: a letter created from an application whose page has an address shows it in "Adresse de l'entreprise", and the preview prints it; a letter whose page and text have none shows the field empty.
Verification: Export: the PDF of a letter created with an address prints it in the window, under the company name.
Verification: `security-review` PASS: the server reading the body of an outside page (allowlist, redirects, size and time bounds); storing page and AI text.
Verification: `code-reviewer` PASS. `ui-expert` is not required, since no UI changes; the e2e covers the rendered field.
FAIL condition: Invented address: an address is stored that is not on the page's structured data and not in the offer's text.
FAIL condition: Partial address: an address without a street, postcode or locality is stored.
FAIL condition: Wrong shape: the stored address is not "street", then "postcode locality", then the country only when it is not Switzerland. Or it repeats the company name.
FAIL condition: Second fetch: the offer's page is fetched more than once per creation, or outside `safeFetch` and the allowlist.
FAIL condition: Blocked creation: a missing address, or a failure while reading it, prevents the letter from being created or changes the route's answer.
FAIL condition: Changed verdict: a closed offer is no longer refused, or an open one is refused.
FAIL condition: Extra cost: the text fallback spends an additional rate-limit unit.
FAIL condition: Scope: another field, another creation path, or an existing letter is changed.
BLOCKER condition: The stub seam cannot serve a page body to the route in tests and e2e without a real network request.
BLOCKER condition: The text fallback cannot be done without an additional rate-limit unit.
BLOCKER condition: A required check cannot run.
Out of scope: Other fields: "Nom du destinataire", "Fonction du destinataire" and "Nom de l'entreprise" are unchanged. The company name is still set as today.
Out of scope: Existing letters: they are not updated. There is no button to look for the address again.
Out of scope: Other creation paths: a letter created by hand, duplicated or translated. The editor's Generate button.
Out of scope: The job application: nothing is stored on it.
Out of scope: Messages: no message tells the user whether an address was found.
Out of scope: Other changes: the job-board allowlist, the availability check's verdicts (a closed offer is still refused as today), `/api/jobs/fetch-external`, and the Destinataire tab's UI.

userStories.title: Otherwise, the address comes from the offer's text
userStories.description: As a job seeker whose offer page gives no address, I want the address found in the offer's text, so that the field is still filled when the text names it.
acceptanceCriteria: When the page gives no complete address (no URL, no structured data, an incomplete address, a host outside the allowlist, a timeout or any other failure), the address is looked for in the application's stored offer text.
An address taken from the text is used only if it appears in the text: its street and its postcode-and-locality are both found there, ignoring case and spacing.
An address found in the text is stored in the same shape as in US-001.
When neither the page nor the text gives a complete address, the letter is created as today and "Adresse de l'entreprise" is empty.
Not finding an address never prevents the letter from being created, and never changes the error the route returns.

FR-2: Order of sources: (1) `hiringOrganization.address` on the offer's page; (2) `jobLocation.address` on the offer's page; (3) the offer's stored text. The first complete address wins.

FR-3: The page is read with the existing `safeFetch` path and job-board allowlist. The read must stay inside the existing time budget and cap how much of the body it reads. Only an HTML answer with a success status is read. The checker's existing verdicts (`gone`, `answered`, `undetermined`) are unchanged.
FR-4: The address is untrusted text: it is cleaned like the other untrusted text this route stores (`sanitizeUntrustedPlainText`); it is capped by the existing `company_address` limit.
FR-5: The text fallback spends no additional unit of the per-user AI rate limit. The creation already spends one.
FR-6: In tests and e2e, the offer page is served by the existing stub seam (`offerPageCheckerFor`); no test reaches a real job board.
FR-7: No new dependency, column, route or migration.
